items.title: Feature-preservation rule, exact-bundle claim boundary, two-bottleneck framing, conservative demand gating, A/B before promotion, positive controls, concrete consumers before abstraction
items.claim: Eleven method principles (listed in CODEX_DISAGREEMENTS §2 table) govern performance work.

The exact-bundle boundary, the two-bottleneck framing, 'unknown consumers force the safe path', 'concrete consumer before an abstraction', and 'a final still cannot certify temporal stability' exist only here and in the CODEX table that links into this file by line number.
items.surviving_record: CLAUDE.md campaign block (feature preservation); QUEUE_2026-08-29_RESEARCH_DISPATCH.md SR-1/SR-6/SR-8; CODEX_DISAGREEMENTS_WITH_FABLE_REVIEW_2026-08-16.md §2 (needs re-anchoring)
items.migrate_text: A measured parity or deficit result belongs to the exact bundle, browser and adapter that produced it (run-performance-campaign.mjs records bundle sha256 at :5566-5572 and adapter identity at :4390) and is never a claim about a later HEAD. WebGPU's steady-state CPU floor and WebGL's first-use link stalls are two optimisation problems and are never collapsed into one 'which renderer is slower' verdict. Attachment or pass gating inventories every consumer, lets an unknown consumer force the safe topology, and asserts demand separately from actual pass opens (the slot-1/scene-colour open counters at WebGPUContext.ts:746-759). Topology or ownership rewrites are promoted only after an interleaved GPU/API/visual A/B; a resource-ownership abstraction is adopted only through one concrete, measured, zero-copy consumer. Optional-path gates carry a feature-on positive control, and temporal behaviour (TAA history, RTE under motion, altitude transitions) is certified by sequences, not a final still.

items.title: WebGPU terrain-buffer lifetime is disconnected from Cesium's quadtree LRU/free lifecycle
items.claim: Terrain GPU buffers are keyed by coordinates only, retained with their CPU arrays, never released from GlobeSurfaceTile.freeResources, and evictStaleResources destroys inline before submit.
items.evidence: WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileBuffers.ts:169-176 getTileKey is `${level}_${x}_${y}`; :577-588 evictStaleResources still calls vertexBuffer.destroy()/indexBuffer.destroy() inline (its host interface at :61 exposes only scheduleTextureDestroy, no buffer retirement); GlobeSurfaceTile.js:158-170 freeResources releases the water-mask texture only, no terrain-buffer lease; TileReplacementQueue.js:49 -> QuadtreeTile.js:611-620 still run before WebGPUContext.endFrame drains _pendingTextureDestroys (:3379). C11-34 (C9-15-TERRAIN-GPU-RESIDENCY-BUDGET / FAR-203) is NOT STARTED (QUEUE_2026-07-18_CAMPAIGN11.md:1669, :2300, :2456); FAR-203 is 'planned' in the ledger (:253-256); DM-09/DM-10 call it 'adjacent'.
items.surviving_record: QUEUE_2026-07-18_CAMPAIGN11.md C11-34 (owner); FAR ledger FAR-203; QUEUE_2026-08-29_RESEARCH_DISPATCH.md DM-09/DM-10 (adjacent)
items.migrate_text: WebGPU terrain realizations live in WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileBuffers.ts keyed by `${level}_${x}_${y}` (:169-176) with no payload revision, context or device generation in the key, and nothing on the quadtree free path releases them: GlobeSurfaceTile.js:158-170 freeResources drops only the water-mask texture, so TileReplacementQueue.trimTiles (:49) frees a tile's CPU side while its GPU buffers stay in _tileBufferCache. The only reclaim is evictStaleResources (:577-588), which destroys buffers inline; because Scene.render calls globe.endFrame before WebGPUContext.endFrame submits, any per-frame use of it can invalidate commands already recorded (the context's _pendingTextureDestroys batch at WebGPUContext.ts:553/:2932/:3379 is the right precedent and has no buffer counterpart). The Batch-731 API lane measured 2,102 buffers created / 561 destroyed over one flight (net +1,541) against WebGL's +5. Owner: C11-34 / FAR-203 (both unstarted); the fix shape is lease release from freeResources / mesh replacement / provider swap / device loss plus post-submit retirement, then a byte-budgeted zero-lease grace LRU - never a per-frame evictStaleResources(visibleTileKeys).

items.title: SceneOctree plane-mask results are compared with Intersect enum values
items.claim: The opt-in octree PVS compares a plane mask against Intersect.OUTSIDE/INSIDE and therefore never culls or short-circuits.
items.evidence: OctreeNode.js:294-300 `visibility = cullingVolume.computeVisibilityWithPlaneMask(...)` then `if (visibility === Intersect.OUTSIDE)`; :322-325 `visibility === Intersect.INSIDE`. CullingVolume.js:196/205 returns MASK_OUTSIDE = 0xffffffff / MASK_INSIDE = 0 while Intersect.js:18 OUTSIDE = -1 (INSIDE = 1), so neither branch can ever match. The code is unchanged since a556f45724; Batches 1133/1149 (C11-62) touched only the dirty-revision rebuild; DEFERRED_WORK.md:10183 NEW-SCENEOCTREE-DIRTY-REVISION-REBUILD-AND-PVS-PROMOTION does not name the enum defect; no queue row does.
items.migrate_text: The opt-in SceneOctree (scene.renderScheduler.octree.enabled) cannot cull: OctreeNode.js:294-300 compares the result of CullingVolume.computeVisibilityWithPlaneMask - MASK_OUTSIDE 0xffffffff / MASK_INSIDE 0 (CullingVolume.js:196/205) - against Intersect.OUTSIDE (-1) and Intersect.INSIDE (1) at :300 and :322-325, so no subtree is ever rejected and the mask short-circuit never fires; the octree merely re-emits every command through a full traversal. Fixing the comparison alone would activate culling with the eligibility, root-bounds, translucent-3D-Tiles, ordering and off-camera shadow-caster semantics still unspecified (the audit's rejected shortcut 8), so the row is 'repair the opt-in semantics as a whole', FIX LATER. Not tracked by any queue row today.

Loss half: WebGPUContext.ts:7657 _clearAllCaches now drains a registered cache registry (_registerResourceCaches) and fires a WebGPUDeviceInvalidationBus; the model cache subscribes (WebGPUModelRenderer.ts:5314) and the culler pool/EDL do, but WebGPULabelRenderer.js and WebGPUPolylineRenderer.js contain no onDeviceInvalidated / device-generation guard (grep), so those per-collection _webgpuCache families still rely on their own scene-format invalidation only. items.migrate_text: Device-loss recovery now runs through a registered cache registry (WebGPUContext.ts:7657 _clearAllCaches, _registerResourceCaches) and a WebGPUDeviceInvalidationBus that the model renderer (WebGPUModelRenderer.ts:5314), culler pool and EDL subscribe to, but the label and polyline collection caches (WebGPULabelRenderer.js:838-871, WebGPUPolylineRenderer.js:1596) subscribe to nothing and carry no device-generation check, so after a recovery they can present old-device pipelines and buffers until a scene-format bump happens to clear them. items.title: OIT composite bind group is rebuilt and its derived-pipeline key is insufficiently specific
items.claim: WebGPUOIT rebuilds the composite bind group every composite and keys derived pipelines by shader length.
items.evidence: WebGPUOIT.ts:259 executeComposite calls _updateCompositeBindGroup() unconditionally and :350-372 createBindGroup()s a fresh 'OIT-Composite-BindGroup' each call; :706 `cacheKey = `${shaderCode.length}_${fragEntry}_${config.label ?? ""}`` (own comment at :381: 'keyed by shader-code length'). OIT is contained default-off under FAR-003 (CesiumDebug.webgpuOIT); FAR-404/FAR-704 (ledger :429-434, :586-594) cover the MSAA topology and dual-source experiment, not this key/reuse defect; DEFERRED_WORK.md:10389-10429 records the flip-evidence gates without it.
items.migrate_text: Before OIT can leave FAR-003 containment its cache identity must be fixed: WebGPUOIT.ts:259 rebuilds the composite bind group on every executeComposite (:350-372 allocates a new GPUBindGroup each frame although the accumulation/revealage views only change on resize or device loss), and derived OIT pipelines are keyed at :706 by shader-code length, fragment entry and label, so two distinct shaders of equal length with the same label alias. Fix: rebuild the composite bind group only when its views change, and key derived pipelines by module identity (the WeakMap-backed webgpuObjectIdentity the central caches use) plus target format, sample count and depth state, then re-run the intersecting-translucency, resize, MSAA, format and device-loss gates. FIX LATER (feature stays reachable, default-off).
